label: Astra: identifying denim shorts and visible construction
Astra: locating source parts on the technical redraw

sourceManifest.subtype: wide-leg shorts with overlapping hip panels
sourceManifest.fit: Wide, flared legs; waistband narrower than the leg openings. Fit on a wearer is unknown.
sourceManifest.construction: The visible garment is a complete pair of front-view shorts. It has a sewn waistband, a central button and fly closure, two continuous main leg panels, broad overlapping hip panels with finished diagonal edges, curved front pocket openings beneath those overlays, two visible belt loops, and turned, topstitched leg hems. The long descending folds in the legs are not treated as additional panel boundaries. The hip overlays are retained above complete main panels rather than subtracted from them. The exposed pocket areas are partly occluded and are review proposals, not confirmed independent fabric cuts. Fly topstitching and hem stitching identify construction details, not additional main-body panels. No hidden pocket bags, zipper teeth, rear components, or unseen belt loops are inferred.
sourceManifest.materialEvidence: Dark indigo-black fabric shows fine diagonal twill texture, characteristic denim surface variation, contrasting brown topstitching, and jeans-style waistband and fly construction. No separate material or colour is established for the hip overlays.
uncertainties: The garment is shown flat without a wearer, so worn fit and exact length classification cannot be established.
The hip overlays obscure portions of the pocket openings and underlying main panels.
The exposed pocket areas may be integral facings rather than separately cut visible pocket pieces; their proposed regions require review.
The fly exterior is visible, but the concealed fastening mechanism and exact facing cut are not.
Hem regions represent turned finishing bands, not separately attached cuffs.

regions.name: Image-left main leg panel
regions.evidence: Continuous denim body from the waistband to the left leg opening; long internal folds have no visible joining seam.

boundary.evidence: Outer side, inner-leg edge and bottom opening are visible garment contours. Upper attachment follows the waistband; occluded portions remain continuous beneath the hip overlay.

regions.name: Image-right main leg panel
regions.evidence: Continuous right leg body below the waistband, with broad folds but no proven additional sewn subdivision.

boundary.evidence: Visible right outer contour, hem edge and inner-leg contour establish the main panel extent; upper portions continue beneath overlapping construction.

regions.name: Image-left exposed front pocket area
regions.evidence: A curved, brown-topstitched pocket opening is visible beneath the diagonal hip overlay; the precise facing construction is occluded.

boundary.evidence: The lower curved opening is supported by visible double topstitching. The other side is occluded by the hip overlay, so this is only a proposed exposed facing region, not an installed fabric cut.

regions.name: Image-right exposed front pocket area
regions.evidence: A curved topstitched front pocket opening appears below the right hip overlay; its upper facing attachment is hidden.

boundary.evidence: Curving brown topstitching supports a pocket opening, while the diagonal overlay hides the opposite attachment. This proposed facing must be reviewed and must not cut the main panel.

regions.name: Front fly exterior
regions.evidence: The center-front overlap and curved J-shaped stitching establish the fly location below the waist button.

boundary.evidence: A center-front folded closure edge is visible, but the curved outer limit is topstitching rather than a proven independent fabric perimeter. Treat this as a review-only fly detail over intact body fabric.

regions.name: Image-left turned leg hem
regions.evidence: A narrow turned hem follows the left opening, with a continuous brown stitch line above the finished lower edge.

boundary.evidence: The lower silhouette and a parallel continuous hem stitch line establish a turned finishing band, not a separate attached panel.

regions.name: Image-right turned leg hem
regions.evidence: The right opening has a narrow turned and topstitched edge, without an attached cuff seam.

boundary.evidence: A visible lower folded edge and parallel brown stitching follow the opening. The upper limit marks hem finishing rather than an independent fabric cut.

regions.name: Front waistband
regions.evidence: A distinct curved band has a finished upper edge and a continuous sewn lower attachment, interrupted by the center-front closure.

boundary.evidence: Upper finished silhouette and lower curved attachment seam are both visible across the front waistband.

regions.name: Image-left overlapping hip panel
regions.evidence: A broad hip piece lies over the pocket and main leg, with a clearly finished, topstitched diagonal free edge descending from the waistband.

boundary.evidence: The diagonal boundary has a finished fabric lip, parallel edge stitching and visible overlap over the pocket. Its outer boundary follows the garment silhouette toward the side.

regions.name: Image-right overlapping hip panel
regions.evidence: A matching broad overlay runs from the waistband across the right hip, with a finished diagonal edge visibly above the pocket and body.

boundary.evidence: The descending edge is supported by a continuous finished lip, edge topstitching and occlusion of the underlying pocket. The outer perimeter follows the visible side silhouette.

regions.name: Image-left front belt loop
regions.evidence: A narrow stitched denim strip crosses the waistband and extends slightly onto the body.

boundary.evidence: Both narrow strip edges and its sewn end are visible above the waistband and hip-panel attachment.

regions.name: Image-right front belt loop
regions.evidence: A second narrow edge-stitched denim strip crosses the waistband to the right of the fly.

boundary.evidence: Visible parallel strip edges, longitudinal stitching and a lower sewn end establish a separate attached belt loop.

regions.name: Center-front waist button
regions.evidence: A round grey, metallic-looking button sits on the waistband at the center-front closure.

boundary.evidence: A distinct circular rim separates the button face from the denim waistband.
